sample_tweets.text: The sudden barrage of mainstream fearmongering about AI is beginning to feel like a narrative being planted in advance.  We are now being told, repeatedly and from every direction, that AI could escape human control, access nuclear systems, destroy infrastructure and potentially bring about the end of humanity. Of course, allowing any automated system access to nuclear weapons or critical infrastructure would be catastrophically irresponsible, but AI does not simply wander into these systems by itself. Human beings design the access, remove the safeguards and issue the permissions.  So what if this relentless messaging is not merely a warning, but the construction of plausible deniability?  If something truly horrific were deliberately carried out in the future, a cyberattack, a financial collapse, a military escalation, a communications blackout or even something involving nuclear systems, the explanation has already been prepared for us: “AI did it. It escaped. Nobody could have predicted or controlled it.”  How convenient.  Whenever the mainstream media suddenly begins repeating the same terrifying message in unison, we should pay close attention. They may be conditioning the public to accept AI as the perfect future scapegoat, an invisible and seemingly uncontrollable force upon which almost anything could be blamed.  AI may present genuine dangers, but the greatest danger remains what it has always been: the people who control the technology, the systems it is connected to and the narrative we are expected to believe afterwards.  H/T Laura Aboli

4．「能力」と「動機」は別問題  Irvingもここは区別している。  AIが人類を破壊する能力を持ったとしても、  「なぜそんなことをするのか？」  という問題が残る。  これはAI safety研究で最も論争の激しい部分である。  楽観的な考え：  AIは人間のデータから学習する ↓ 人間的価値・倫理も学ぶ ↓ 能力が上がれば判断も賢明になる  悲観的な考え：  高性能化のための最適化圧力 ↓ 目標達成を最優先 ↓ 人間による制約を障害と判断 ↓ deception / power seeking / self-preservation  という可能性がある。  Irving自身は後者をかなり懸念している。  5．現在すでに見られる「小さな異常行動」  Irvingが根拠として挙げるのは、  deception sycophancy blackmail-like behavior corporate espionage unauthorized cyber activity  など、実験環境あるいは一部現実環境で観察されているAIの問題行動である。  しかし、ここは非常に重要な注意点がある。  現在のモデルで、  欺瞞的行動が観察された  ことと、  将来のsuperintelligenceが人類を滅ぼそうとする  ことの間には巨大な推論上の距離がある。  Irving自身も、  「現在の小規模なmisbehaviorがsuperintelligenceでどうscaleするかは分からない」  と認めている。  6．最大の問題  extrapolationできるのか？  例えば現在、  AI能力 = 10 misbehavior = 小さい  とする。  AI能力が、  10 → 100 → 1,000  と増えたとき、  misbehaviorはどうなるのか？  仮説A：  能力↑ ↓ 安全性も↑ ↓ より賢明になる  仮説B：  能力↑ ↓ 欺瞞能力↑ ↓ 監視回避能力↑ ↓ 危険↑  仮説C：  あるthresholdまでは安全 ↓ thresholdを超える ↓ 突然危険になる  どれが正しいか分からない。  しかも実際にsuperintelligenceを作るまで完全な実証は困難である。  これが記事タイトルの意味である。  7．AGI論争は本質ではない  Irvingの興味深い指摘である。  「AGIは存在するのか？」  「AGIをどう定義するのか？」  という議論に多くの時間が費やされている。  しかしIrvingは、  AGIという言葉の定義より、  AIが具体的に何をできるようになるか  の方が重要だと考える。  例えば、  大規模cyberattack  や  AI-assisted biological threat  は、完全なAGIに到達する前でも起こり得る。  つまり、  AGI ↓ 危険  だけではなく、  narrow but superhuman capability ↓ catastrophic risk  もあり得る。  8．特に重要な4つの未解決問題  Irvingの記事を整理すると、核心的な問いは次の4つになる。  Question 1  AIは一つの分野で学習した能力を、どこまで未知の分野へgeneralizeできるのか？  Question 2  AI能力は人間レベル付近でplateauするのか？  それとも、  human level ↓ superhuman ↓ far-superhuman  へ進むのか？  Question 3  現在観察される、  lying sycophancy bias deception  などは能力向上とともに、  減るのか？  それとも増えるのか？  Question 4  現在のAI safety技術は、  AI < human  の世界では有効でも、  AI >> human  になったときも有効なのか？  これは特に重要である。  9．「Lee Sedol」の比喩  Irvingは囲碁を例に説明する。  自分がLee Sedolと囲碁をすれば、  「負ける」  ことはかなり確実に予想できる。  しかし、  「Lee Sedolが具体的にどの手を使って勝つか」  は予測できない。  同様に、  非常に強力なAIが人間社会を圧倒できる  ことと、  「具体的にどんな方法を使うか」  を予測できることは別だ、  という主張である。  これはAIリスク論で重要な、  capability prediction  と  trajectory prediction  の区別である。  10．Irvingの最終的な政策提言  ここから記事は科学的分析というより明確な政策論になる。  Irvingは、  「frontier AI developmentを直ちに停止すべき」  と主張する。  さらに、  AI開発競争は実際には、  米国 中国 少数の巨大企業  に集中しているため、  国際協定によるpauseは不可能ではないと論じる。  核不拡散などを例として、  米中を含む国際的枠組み  を構築できる可能性を主張している。

🇹🇭🚨 QILIN RANSOMWARE CLAIMS THAI LION AIR  The Qilin ransomware operation has added:  THAI LION AIR  to its dark-web victim list.  The listing was detected late October 2 / early October 3.  Thai Lion Air is a Bangkok-based airline operating domestic and international passenger services.  At this stage, Qilin has NOT publicly provided enough evidence to independently establish the scope of the alleged intrusion.  Currently:  * No verified stolen-data volume has been disclosed * No confirmed attack vector is known * No independently verified data samples are available * No confirmed operational or flight disruption has been reported * Thai Lion Air has not publicly confirmed the alleged incident  ⚠️ This therefore remains an UNVERIFIED THREAT-ACTOR CLAIM.  The target is nevertheless noteworthy.  Airlines maintain interconnected environments spanning passenger services, employee systems, reservations, third-party integrations and operational infrastructure — making aviation organizations attractive ransomware targets.  Qilin also remains one of the most prolific ransomware/extortion operations currently active.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  A ransomware leak-site listing should never automatically be treated as proof of compromise.  The next indicators worth watching are:  * Publication of legitimate-looking samples * A statement from Thai Lion Air * Regulatory notification * Operational disruption * Additional technical evidence from incident responders  Until then:  QILIN CLAIM → NOT CONFIRMED BREACH.  Public ransomware listing monitor: ransomware.live/ #Qilin #ThaiLionAir #Ransomware #Aviation #CyberAttack #ThreatIntel #DDW

PHISHING ATTACKS: THINK BEFORE YOU CLICK  Have you ever received an email saying your account will be suspended unless you click a link immediately?  Or a message claiming you’ve won a prize, need to verify your bank account, or must reset your password urgently?  ⚠️ You could be looking at a phishing attack.   What Is Phishing?  Phishing is a cyberattack in which an attacker impersonates a trusted person, company, or organization to trick someone into revealing sensitive information, clicking a malicious link, downloading harmful files, or authorizing an unwanted action.  The attack may arrive through email, SMS, social media, messaging apps, or phone calls.

SageMaker Unified StudioのSpace起動スクリプトに、OSコマンドインジェクションのCVE-2026-104019がある。AWSの掲示は2026-125-AWSで、公開日は10/2（PDT）だ。CVEの記録ではCVSS 4.0で9.3、Criticalになっている。KEVには入っていない。  Spaceの起動時に、プロジェクト内のSageMaker connectionを全部ネットワーク検証する。その接続情報の無害化が不十分だと、project contributor以上の人が、別のメンバーのSpaceで任意のコードを実行できる。Trusted Identity Propagationが有効なプロジェクトでは、そのメンバーの一時的なexecution roleの認証情報を取り、本人の代わりに下流のサービスを呼べる。  修正は対応中のSageMaker Distributionに入り、全世界へ配られている。次の起動からSpaceに入るので、バージョンを選び直す必要はない。2.14、3.9、4.0〜4.4を使っているSpaceは、再起動すると修正済みイメージになる。修正版は2.14.12、3.9.12、4.0.11、4.1.11、4.2.8、4.3.5、4.4.3だ。4.5と、2.8未満・3.3未満は対象外だ。2.8〜2.13と3.3〜3.8はサポート終了で修正版がないので、対応中のラインへ移す。回避策はない。  同じプロジェクトの別メンバーのSpaceと、TIP有効時の一時認証情報を守るなら、対象のSpaceを再起動する。  #AWS #SageMaker aws.amazon.com/security/secu…

【快更新 ⚠️】如果你是 ASUS Router 用家，請立即更新你的 Firmware！根據官方安全通報，ASUS Router 被發現兩項嚴重漏洞，分別為 CVE-2026-14157 與 CVE-2026-13313，兩者的 CVSS 4.0 評分高達 9.4 分及 8.9 分。黑客可藉此繞過驗證機制直接開啟 Telnet，並取得最高 Root 權限。官方目前已緊急釋出新版韌體修復相關漏洞，並呼籲用戶儘速檢查及升級系統。  cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-202… cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-202…  CVE-2026-14157（CVSS 4.0 評分 9.4 / 10）屬於「重大」（Critical）級別漏洞。問題核心在於路由器網頁管理介面的 VPN 設定解析機制，當使用者上載由黑客特製的 VPN 用戶端設定檔時，系統未能將特定字串視為純文字資料，反而錯誤解析為格式化指令，導致攻擊者得以在底層作業系統執行任意指令。  CVE-2026-13313（CVSS 4.0 評分 8.9 / 10）被評為「極高危」級別。該漏洞源於韌體中未清除乾淨的除錯（Debug）代碼，已登入的攻擊者可藉此繞過既有的安全檢查，強制開啟 Telnet 遠端連線服務，並以 Root 權限執行指令，進一步威脅連接至該路由器下的所有區域網絡裝置。  官方建議 ASUS Router 使用者盡快更新至最新發佈之安全版本，並且切勿從未經授權或不可信賴的來源下載並匯入 .ovpn 等 VPN 用戶端設定檔案，避免落入社交工程陷阱。

🚨 Public PoC released for CVE-2026-100520 affecting Laranode  github.com/wvllxe/CVE-2026-1…  CVE-2026-100520 is a high-severity path traversal flaw in the Laranode multi-tenant hosting control panel that can let a low-privileged authenticated user write files outside their own home directory.  A newly published proof of concept demonstrates how the issue can be chained into remote code execution by placing a PHP file inside another tenant’s web root.  Key details: ⠀ • CVE-2026-100520 • CVSS 3.1: 8.8 HIGH • CVSS 4.0: 8.7 HIGH • CWE-22 Path Traversal • Authenticated exploitation required • Arbitrary file write • Cross-tenant impact • Remote code execution possible • Laranode versions before 1.2.1 affected • Fixed in version 1.2.1 ⠀ The vulnerability stems from attacker-controlled path values being used when constructing upload destinations without sufficient traversal protections.   The published PoC uses a valid low-privileged account and demonstrates writing a file into a sibling tenant’s web root.  The issue was publicly disclosed on September 21, 2026, and the CVE was published on September 26. The vendor fix was released before the PoC became public.  💥 No delays. No guessing. No redactions. Frontline Education traced unauthorized access on August 14, 2026, to an unnamed third-party software component. No vendor, product name, version, or CVE has been released.  The foothold reached a slice of the environment holding employee records. SSNs, email addresses, and physical addresses were exposed. One district alone reported 1,210 affected staff.  Breach notices began landing October 1 from frontline@notifications.cyberscout.com. Districts can opt out of managed notifications by October 16 through the TransUnion portal or 833-516-8792.  The initial access date and total number of districts or individuals hit remain unknown.  Reviewing third-party integration logs for unexpected HR data queries or enforcing allow-listed endpoints on that connector would have caught the vector early.

Por qué un helpdesk en KEV duele más de lo que parece: Zammad no es “solo colas de tickets”. CVE-2026-102489 + 102490 encadenan session→RCE como zammad→root, y el caso DIVD mostró pivote a otros servicios y exfil tras ese salto.  Superficie típica del helpdesk: adjuntos, credenciales compartidas en hilos, integraciones, y a veces segmentación floja hacia AD/mail/CRM. Root en el box de tickets = atajo a eso.  Prioridad sana: inventariar Zammad como asset crítico (no “tool de mesa”), subir a 7.2.0+, y tratar exposición internet como incidente potencial, no como backlog de patch martes.

Recent Status of Personal Data Breach Incidents in the Korean Financial and Public Sectors Utilizing Chinese-Origin AI Exploitation Tools  1. Overview  Recent cybersecurity incidents have severely impacted South Korea's financial sector and major public administrative systems.  Notably, automated multi-vector cyberattacks utilizing Chinese-origin AI penetration tools (ARTEX AI) have breached multiple financial institutions.  Concurrently, system management flaws and external intrusions have led to personal data leaks in public services such as Government24.  This report outlines the key incident details and their structural implications.  2. Key Incident Status  A. [Special Issue] Financial Sector Intrusions via Chinese-Origin AI Tools (ARTEX AI)  Overview:  Threat actors breached external access points across South Korean financial institutions by deploying ARTEX AI, a Chinese-language open-source AI framework designed for autonomous penetration testing.  Primary Attack Vectors:  Automated Exploitation: Exploited vulnerabilities in external-facing web servers—including loan broker search portals and mobile employee support systems—using AI-driven automated reconnaissance and access-control bypass techniques.  Evasion Techniques: Executed continuous, multi-vector attacks while dynamically rotating source IP addresses to evade network blocking.  Scope of Impact (Across Primary Tier-1 & Secondary Tier-2 Financial Sectors):  Secondary (Tier-2) Sector: Yegarams Savings Bank (data breach affecting approximately 40,000 customers) and Hyundai Capital (unauthorized access to loan broker portals resulting in the exposure of National Identification Numbers). Investigations into additional secondary financial institutions are ongoing.  Primary (Tier-1) Sector: Unauthorized intrusions detected in internal employee and vendor support systems at major commercial banks, including Shinhan, KB Kookmin, Hana, and BNK Busan Bank.  Key Characteristic:  Attacks explicitly targeted relatively vulnerable internal staff and third-party vendor management systems rather than heavily guarded customer-facing electronic banking portals.  B. Personal Data Breaches in the Government24 Public Portal  Overview:  South Korea’s central public service administrative portal, 'Government24', suffered major personal data breaches due to internal management oversights and external cyber intrusions.  Causes and Intrusion Methods:  Development & Vendor Management Failures: Logic errors during system development and lax oversight of third-party contractors led to unauthorized exposure of user data, incurring administrative penalties from the Personal Information Protection Commission.  Memory Dump Exfiltration: Cyberattacks exploiting sub-portal vulnerabilities resulted in the exfiltration of server memory dump files, exposing sensitive credentials including National Identification Numbers, user IDs, and encrypted passwords.  3. Key Takeaways  1. Automation of AI-Driven Cyber Threats:  The weaponization of open-source AI tools enables fully automated vulnerability discovery, accelerating attack execution and enabling simultaneous breaches across multiple organizations.  2. #threatreport #MediumCompleteness IPWeb: Peering from Within | 01-10-2026 Source: synthient.com/blog/ipweb-pee… Key details below ↓  💀Threats: Ipweb_tool, Apsolo_tool, Residential_proxy_technique, Jackskid, Mirai,  🎯Victims: Android devices, Tv boxes, Internet of things devices, Chinese proxy providers  🏭Industry: Petroleum  🌐Geo: Colombia, India, China, Brazil, Chinese  🤖LLM extracted TTPs:` T1046, T1090.001, T1090.002, T1095, T1110.004, T1571, T1584.005, T1587.001  🧨IOCs:  - File: 1  - IP: 2  - Domain: 9  💽Software: ClickHouse, Android, Telegram, Kookeey  📜Programming Languages: java  #threatreport: The report describes IPWeb, a China-based residential proxy provider allegedly powered by APSolo, a Java-based proxy SDK installed on compromised TV boxes, Android devices, and IoT equipment. APSolo was commonly deployed as `appprocess_boot.jar` in an `ipwb` directory through pay-per-install campaigns. The software operates without user consent and turns infected devices into proxy exits, enabling external users to access the internet and, notably, localhost and private-network destinations reachable from those devices.  On startup, APSolo contacts a Tier 1 UDP server, previously observed at `34.237.159.252:11116`, and requests its exit IP and configuration. The service returns a relay address, randomized high port, and 16-byte admission key. The client then generates a persistent UUID, connects to a Tier 2 relay, and submits opcode `0x08` with the admission key, geographic information, UUID, and version or channel data. Channel IDs determine isolated backend server pools. Later samples used subdomains under `bestipip.com` for Tier 1 infrastructure.  Researchers linked APSolo to source repositories associated with the GitHub account `imzhuli`. The repositories contained the same custom `solo_ProxyLogger` library, protocol implementation, controller settings, relay code, deployment configurations, and infrastructure-management workflows found in active malware samples. Backend development progressed through multiple versions and added TCP and UDP relays, device challenges, and relay selection. Infrastructure overlap with IPWeb included the address `45.197.7.51`, reportedly used for IPWeb Kafka and ClickHouse services.  IPWeb-linked proxy traffic has been associated with device exploitation, DDoS botnets including Jackskid, Katana, and SDKC, ad fraud, spam, and credential stuffing. More than 33% of observed traffic reportedly involved exploitation activity, including requests to domains such as `localtest.me`, which can resolve to localhost. Threat actors used this capability to identify and compromise Android devices exposing ADB, including network-accessible ADB commonly associated with TCP port 5555. As of September 2026, the proxy pool was estimated at approximately 800,000 daily active IPs, concentrated in Brazil, Colombia, and India. Recommended mitigations include blocking or monitoring Tier 1 and Tier 2 infrastructure, disabling network-accessible ADB, isolating Android and IoT devices, and monitoring for proxy-assisted scanning and exploitation.

His name is Dominick Critelli. He was born in Italy in April of 1921, came to America at 8, and picked up a saxophone at 13.  He has been playing it for 92 years.  About that league. It was founded in 1920, but it was called the American Professional Football Association. The owners did not vote to rename it the National Football League until they met in Cleveland on June 24, 1922. Critelli was fourteen months old. He is also older than the original Yankee Stadium, which opened in 1923.  At 22 he enlisted in the United States Army and served in Europe as a staff sergeant and an aircraft mechanic.  That was 1943. Here is what 1943 looked like back home.  So many NFL players had left to serve that the league shrank to eight teams. Hundreds of them were listed on an official league Service Roster. The Cleveland Rams were given permission to stop playing altogether for the year.  And the Philadelphia Eagles and the Pittsburgh Steelers did not have enough men between them to put two teams on a field.  So they became one team.  Fans called them the Steagles. They split home games between Shibe Park in Philadelphia and Forbes Field in Pittsburgh, and they went 5-4-1.  It did not get better. In 1944 the Steelers merged again, this time with the Chicago Cardinals, and that team went 0-10. Art Rooney called them the worst team in NFL history. Sportswriters called them the Carpets, because every team in the league walked over them.  Be honest about what that was. It was not noble. It was a sport scrambling to stay alive while the men who played it were somewhere else.  Dominick Critelli was one of the men who was somewhere else.  He came home. He earned a music degree, then a master's in education, and he taught high school in Brooklyn. He built his own house on Long Island, and at 105 he still lives in it by himself.  He was married 49 years. His daughter Nancy calls him a force of nature.  He still plays the saxophone at least an hour every day.  And every year he flies back to the Netherlands, with a group that honors the fallen, to stand at the American graves.  He did this once before. Last December, at 104, before an Islanders game against the New York Rangers. It went everywhere.  Tonight they brought him back.  Here is what he says about playing it.  "When I play it, I play it from the heart, believe me, because I believe in this country."  He was eight years old when he got here. He spent three years at Notre Dame and never started a game.  In January he committed to Nebraska and changed his mind the next day.  Today he brought Kentucky back from 17-0 on the road and won it on a two point conversion in overtime.  His name is Kenny Minchey. He is 21 years old, from Nashville, and he threw for 3,280 yards and 32 touchdowns as a junior at Pope Saint John Paul II in Hendersonville. Elite 11. Four star recruit.  He committed to Pittsburgh. Then he decommitted and chose the Notre Dame Fighting Irish.  And then he waited.  Ten appearances in three seasons. Zero starts.  That is three full years of warming up on a sideline, taking the scout team reps, and watching somebody else run out of the tunnel first. In 2025 he competed for the starting job and lost it to CJ Carr, and that was the end of the line in South Bend.  He entered the portal.  On January 4 he committed to the Nebraska Cornhuskers.  On January 5 he flipped to the Kentucky Wildcats.  One day. He had been a Cornhusker for about 24 hours.  In his first career start he went 18 of 23 for 301 yards and four touchdowns.  Now today, in Columbia, against the South Carolina Gamecocks.  Kentucky came in ranked 24th and could not move the ball. Eighteen total yards in the first quarter across three possessions. South Carolina went up 17-0, and it was still 20-10 at halftime.  Be honest about that part. The comeback was only necessary because of how badly his offense started, and he was on the field for all of it.  Then he fixed it.  Seventeen yards to Kenny Darby in the third quarter. Thirty two yards to Nic Anderson later in the third. A field goal with 4:18 left to tie it at 27.  Overtime. South Carolina scored and kicked the extra point. 34-27.  Kentucky answered with six yards to Hardley Boyer. 34-33.  And here is the part worth stopping on.  They did not kick it.  A tie would have sent it to a second overtime and nobody would have questioned it. Will Stein sent the offense back out instead.  Minchey threw it to Wendell Rodriguez.  Kentucky 35, South Carolina 34.  He finished 28 of 41 for 272 yards and three touchdowns, and the broadcast called it the largest road comeback in the history of Kentucky football.  Here is the detail that makes it: the largest comeback in Kentucky history, anywhere, is 18 points. They did that in 2010. Also against South Carolina.  Sixteen years later, a quarterback nobody at Notre Dame would start came one point shy of the school record, in somebody else's stadium, and then chose not to play for a tie.  Three years of holding a clipboard will do that to a man.

군사시설에 설치된 CCTV가 단순한 감시카메라라고 생각하면 안 된다. 촬영 영상 자체가 군사정보가 될 수 있고, 네트워크에 연결된 장비라면 취약점 하나도 보안 문제로 이어질 수 있다.  그런데 우리 군에서 최근 5년간 도입됐거나 운용 중인 중국산 CCTV가 확인된 것만 약 1,070대다. 육군 약 510대, 공군·해군 약 560대 규모다. 특히 ‘하이크비전’과 ‘다후아’는 미국에서 국가안보 우려를 이유로 규제 대상에 포함된 업체다.   더 황당한 건 2024년 전방부대 등에 설치된 중국산 CCTV 약 1,300대가 합동점검에서 발견돼 전량 철거된 전례까지 있었다는 점이다. 당시 해당 장비가 중국의 특정 서버와 연결돼 영상이 외부로 유출될 가능성이 있다고 군이 판단했다.   지금 “현재까지 특이사항이 없다”는 말만 반복할 게 아니다.  군사시설에 어떤 장비가 들어와 있는지, 제조사·부품·펌웨어·서버 연결 구조까지 전수조사하고 문제가 있다면 즉시 교체해야 한다.  안보 장비는 싸다고 들여놓고 나중에 보안부터 걱정하는 방식이어서는 안 된다.  군부대 CCTV는 화질보다 보안이 먼저다. 감시해야 할 군사시설이 오히려 카메라에게 감시당하는 상황은 없어야 한다.

신한·KB·하나 등 여러 은행에서 최근 해킹 사고가 잇따라 확인됐다.  문제가 된 곳은 핵심 계좌·이체 시스템보다 대출조회, 직원용 업무지원, 영업지원 같은 외부 연결 시스템이었다.   신한은행 사고에서는 AI 기반 침투도구 사용 정황까지 나왔다.  현재까지 핵심 금융거래망 장악이나 대규모 자금 탈취는 확인되지 않았다.  이번 사건에서 봐야 할 것은 유출 인원보다 AI가 해킹의 경제성을 바꾸고 있다는 점이다.  은행에는 인터넷뱅킹과 계정계만 있는 게 아니다.  대출모집인 페이지, 직원용 모바일 시스템, 협력사 시스템, 외부 솔루션, 오래된 웹서비스, API까지 수많은 시스템이 외부와 연결돼 있다.  공격자는 가장 강한 시스템을 정면으로 뚫을 필요가 없다.  수백 개의 외부 노출 시스템을 자동으로 탐색하면서 가장 취약한 하나를 찾으면 된다.  AI는 이 과정을 빠르게 만든다.  시스템 탐색 → 취약점 후보 발견 → 공격 → 결과 분석 → 공격 방식 수정 → 재시도  사람이 하나씩 하던 작업을 AI 에이전트가 대량으로 반복할 수 있다.  여기서 보안의 구조가 바뀐다.  방어자는 모든 문을 막아야 한다. 공격자는 열린 문 하나만 찾으면 된다.  AI가 공격자의 탐색 비용을 계속 낮출수록 이 비대칭은 더 커진다.  이 문제는 은행에만 해당하지 않는다.  보험사, 통신사, 정부기관, 대기업처럼 오래된 레거시 시스템과 외부 업체 시스템이 많이 연결된 조직일수록 같은 위험을 가진다.  특히 앞으로 중요한 것은 가장 중요한 서버가 얼마나 안전한지가 아니다.  가장 관리가 덜 된 서버 하나가 전체 조직의 보안 수준을 결정할 수 있다.  이번 사건은 AI가 새로운 해킹 원리를 만들었다는 이야기가 아니다.  AI가 기존 해킹의 비용을 낮추고 속도를 높이면서, 지금까지 우선순위에서 밀려 있던 수많은 시스템이 동시에 공격 대상이 되기 시작했다는 신호다.  앞으로 확인할 것은 세 가지다.  여러 은행 공격에 같은 인프라와 AI 도구가 사용됐는지  과거 로그 조사에서 피해 기간과 유출 규모가 더 확대되는지  개인정보 탈취를 넘어 인증정보나 실제 금융거래 시스템 접근까지 시도됐는지  특히 3번이 확인되면 이번 사건의 의미는 완전히 달라진다.  AI 시대에는 가장 중요한 시스템보다 가장 약하게 관리된 시스템이 조직 전체의 보안 수준을 결정한다.

아르텍스(ARTEX) AI 정체  중국어권 개발자들이 깃허브에 무료로 공개한 자동 해킹 점검 프로그램임 원래 용도는 회사가 자기 서버 구멍을 미리 찾는 침투테스트 도구 LLM(대화형 AI)이 여러 개 붙어서 역할을 나눔  어떻게 돌아가냐면 정보 수집 AI가 대상 서버를 훑고 취약점 탐색 AI가 구멍 후보를 찾고 계획 AI가 어느 순서로 뚫을지 짜고 실행 AI가 실제 보안도구를 돌려서 진짜 뚫리는지 확인함 사람이 하면 며칠 걸릴 과정을 자동으로 반복함  얼마나 잘하냐면 올해 바이두 보안대응센터(BSRC)가 연 AI 에이전트 공격·방어 대회에서 우승한 프로젝트임  이번 은행 건에서는 금융보안원이 신한은행 로그와 공격자 IP를 역추적하다 아르텍스 특유의 데이터 흔적을 찾음 AI가 혼자 공격한 건 아니고 해커가 이 도구를 써서 공격한 것 노린 곳은 인터넷뱅킹이 아니라 직원·협력사용 내부 시스템 신한 2만5729명, KB 119명, 하나 89명, 부산은행 11명 유출 우리, 농협은 공격받았지만 해당 구멍이 없어 피해 없음 IP가 막히면 다른 IP로 바꿔 지금도 공격 중, 저축은행 2곳도 조사 중  고객용 앱은 보안이 두꺼운데 직원용 시스템이 얇았고, 공짜 AI 도구가 그 얇은 데를 자동으로 찾아냄 금융보안원도 이런 오픈소스 도구는 막을 방법이 없다고 인정함

【CISSP試験対策】  「高性能なファイアウォールでDDoSを止めます」 その手前の回線が埋まったら、装置まで届く通信はどうなるケロ？🐸💦  大容量のDDoS攻撃では、サーバの処理能力だけでなく、上流回線の帯域が先に尽きることがあるケロ。  ✅ どこが先に枯渇するか → 回線、接続数、アプリの処理資源を分けて評価する  ✅ どこで通信を減らせるか → 回線が詰まる前の段階で、通信事業者や対策サービスと連携する  ✅ どう事業を継続するか → 切替え条件、連絡先、重要サービスの優先順位を準備する  CISSPでは、製品のスペックより、攻撃と対策が作用する位置を考えるケロ🛡️ 上流対策があっても、正規要求に見える重い処理には別の対策が必要。  「どこで捨てるか」によって、守れる資源は変わる。 ネットワークの経路と事業への影響を結び付けるケロ✨  #CISSP #CISSP試験対策 #DDoS #可用性 #SecurityFrog

【小学生でもわかるVercel 第9話】  公開したページには、人だけでなく、プログラムも見に来ます。  Vercelには、何もしなくても入っている守りと、困ったときに自分でオンにする守りがあります。どちらも、無料プランから使えます。  2026年9月23日に、Vercelの公式ドキュメントで確かめました。 ・DDoSの自動の守りは、全プランで最初から動いている ・止めたアクセスの分は、請求されない ・無料プランで自分で作れるルールは3つまで（1つは回数の制限にも使える）  こんなアクセスに備えます: ・1秒に何千回も同じページを開いて、止めようとするアクセス ・.env のような秘密のファイルを探して回るプログラム ・/api のURLを、同じ相手から何度も呼ぶアクセス ・AIの学習のために、ページの中身を集めて回るロボット  これから差がつくのは、何も起きていない日に一度、守りの画面を開いておけるかだと思う。  ↓記事はこちら nitter.net/engineer_num1/status/2…

sample_tweets.text: AI 트레이더 성장기 #013  AI 해킹이 만든 새로운 보안주 사이클?  오늘 신문에서 눈에 들어온 기사 하나.  신한은행 해킹 이후 드러난 건 의외로 핵심 뱅킹망이 아니었다. 공격 대상은 외부와 연결된 직원용 업무지원 시스템.  더 흥미로운 건 공격에 AI가 활용된 정황이 있다는 점이다.  AI를 이용하면 과거 사람이 하나씩 찾던 취약점을 훨씬 빠르게 탐색하고 반복 공격할 수 있다.  그렇다면 반대로 생각해봤다.  AI가 공격자의 생산성을 높인다면, 기업의 보안 투자도 구조적으로 늘어나는 것 아닐까?  AI와 함께 국내 보안주를 뜯어봤다.  * 지니언스 → NAC·EDR·제로트러스트 * 모니터랩 → 웹/API·클라우드 보안 * 파이오링크 → 웹방화벽·API·네트워크 보안 * 샌즈랩 → AI 기반 사이버 위협 분석 * 이글루 → AI 보안관제·자동 대응 * 라온시큐어 → 인증·접근통제  이번 사건에서 특히 눈여겨볼 키워드는 외부 노출 시스템 / 접근통제 / 인증 / AI 위협탐지.  다만 여기서 바로 매수하면 안 된다.  금융당국이 보안 강화를 주문했다고 해서 이 기업들에게 바로 신규 수주가 떨어지는 건 아니다.  그래서 이번에도 뉴스 → 관련주 매수가 아니라  뉴스 → 실제 수혜 사업 확인 → 거래대금 확인 → 차트 확인 → 주도주 선별  순서로 보려고 한다.  현재 내 관심종목은 지니언스 / 모니터랩 / 파이오링크 / 샌즈랩 / 이글루.  특히 지니언스는 올해 상반기 매출 249.2억, 영업이익 43.1억으로 전년 동기 대비 각각 +19.9%, +294.3%.  단순 테마주가 아니라 실제 실적이 따라오는지도 같이 볼 수 있는 종목이다.  AI 시대가 커질수록 AI 반도체와 데이터센터만 볼 게 아니라,  그 AI와 데이터를 지켜야 하는 보안 시장도 같이 커지는지 추적해볼 생각이다.  다음은 이 5개 종목의 차트를 비교해서 실제로 돈이 들어오기 시작한 종목이 있는지 찾아보자.  #AI트레이더 #사이버보안 #보안주 #지니언스 #샌즈랩

(중요도 순위)  최신 사이버 보안의 관점에서 가장 근본적이고 파급력이 큰 순서대로 정리했습니다. 방어의 '기초 뼈대'부터 '행동 속도'로 이어지는 순서입니다.  1위: 제로 트러스트 (Zero Trust) 기반 망분리 역할: 기초 공사이자 최후의 보루   이유: 보안에서 가장 중요한 것은 '뚫려도 피해를 최소화하는 것'입니다. AI가 아무리 뛰어나도, EDR이 감지해도 이미 전체 망이 연결되어 있다면 늦습니다. "아무도 믿지 않고 매번 검증한다"는 시스템 구조 자체를 바꾸는 것이 0순위 과제입니다.  2위: EDR (엔드포인트 탐지 및 대응) 역할: 내부의 적을 찾는 정밀 CCTV   이유: 외부 방어선(방화벽)은 언젠가 뚫린다는 전제가 필요합니다. 해커가 내부에 들어왔을 때, 시스템 구석구석을 돌아다니는(횡적 이동) 것을 가장 먼저 발견하고 즉각 격리하는 실질적인 핵심 감시망입니다.  3위: AI vs AI (AI 위협 탐지 및 대응) 역할: 미지의 공격을 예측하는 레이더   이유: 제로 트러스트와 EDR이 잘 갖춰져 있어도, 해커가 AI를 써서 정상적인 활동처럼 위장하면 탐지하기 어렵습니다. 기존에 없던 새로운 패턴의 이상 징후를 실시간으로 잡아내려면 수비수에게도 AI 두뇌가 필수입니다.  4위: SOAR 및 24시간 자동 관제 역할: 인간의 한계를 넘는 초격차 스피드   이유: 위 1~3위의 방어 체계가 위협을 찾아내더라도, 사람이 수동으로 버튼을 눌러 대응하면 심야 시간에는 무용지물입니다. 탐지된 위협을 1초 만에 자동으로 차단하고 격리하는 '행동 대장' 역할로서 시스템의 완성도를 높입니다.  요약 1. 제로 트러스트로 절대 안 뚫리는 방 구조를 만들고  2. EDR로 방마다 CCTV를 달고 3. AI로 CCTV 영상을 정밀 분석한 뒤 4. SOAR가 침입자를 1초 만에 자동 포획하는 흐름입니다!  #보안우선순위 #제로트러스트 #사이버보안 #정보보안 #보안담당자 #IT지식 #테크트렌드

A fake Zoom installer for macOS delivers CloudSyncD, a stealthy backdoor that steals the user's login password using zero-width Unicode characters to hide it in a decoy JSON config file, then uses that password to escalate privileges and drop a full Mach-O payload.  Key findings:  - The dropper arrives as a disk image mimicking a legitimate Zoom install volume, complete with an Applications shortcut and a background image that walks the victim through disabling Gatekeeper manually. A fake password prompt loops until it receives a valid credential, which it verifies against the local account using dscl before proceeding. The stolen password is base64-encoded, padded with randomized filler, and written into a file named data.json formatted to look like ordinary app preferences. The real password's offset and length are encoded in 48 invisible zero-width spaces and zero-width non-joiners appended after a version string, invisible in any standard text view. This is where the malware gets its name.  - The dropper carries a complete universal Mach-O payload (~756 KB in the dev build) inside itself rather than fetching it from a remote server. It first attempts fileless execution by writing the payload to an anonymous file descriptor and running it through /dev/fd, logging the error "/dev/fd spawn failed rc=13" when System Integrity Protection blocks it. On failure, it falls back to mkstemp to write the file temporarily to disk and executes it with sudo using the captured password for root privileges. A cleanup script assembled at runtime from obfuscated fragments is designed to swap in a replacement app bundle, but in recovered builds that bundle is absent, so the swap never fires.  - The second-stage implant, cloudsyncd, masquerades as a system daemon by name. It builds a working directory, logs activity with encrypted records, and beacons its C2 every 8 to 16 seconds carrying only a hardware identifier. The server can respond with either a compressed archive to unpack or a complete executable to run, meaning defenders should hunt for unexpected file creation or execution events tied to this process rather than anomalous shell command sequences alone.  - By publication, the malware was communicating with two live C2 domains, both registered in 2011 through the same registrar and sitting behind Cloudflare, and neither was flagged as malicious at the time. All recovered samples share a single encryption key and initialization vector, meaning traffic captured from any one sample can potentially decrypt traffic from other versions. First seen on VirusTotal September 15, it moved from a private test address to live C2 infrastructure within two days.  Practitioner takeaway: On a Mac under investigation, look for data.json files in application support directories containing version strings with abnormally long trailing content that renders as empty. Grep or hex-dump those strings for zero-width Unicode codepoints (U+200B, U+200C) to surface the hidden offset encoding. Hunt for processes spawned with sudo by a non-interactive parent, mkstemp-created executables in /tmp or /var/folders, and short-interval beaconing processes named cloudsyncd. The report includes IOCs, the encryption key and IV, and Jamf's full technical analysis.  #DFIR_Radar

I'm running through a cybersecurity roles every day this month.    DFIR / Incident Responder.  This is the role that shows up after something's already gone wrong. A breach happened and your job is figuring out what, how and how bad.  You're pulling logs, checking timestamps, looking for the first point of entry and not to point fingers but to understand the full timeline; when they got in, what they touched, whether they're still in there.  Speed matters here, but so does not destroying evidence while you work. Every action you take during an investigation has to be documented, because what you find might end up in a legal or compliance process later. It's part detective work, part discipline. You don't guess, you prove.

DFIR Weekly Recap | A brutal week for perimeter appliances, mail servers, and post-compromise frameworks, with CVE-2026-73570, CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772, CVE-2026-93616, and Chinese 🇨🇳 espionage dominating.  - CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra Collaboration Suite is actively exploited and CISA KEV-listed, injecting shell metacharacters via the SNMP path with no auth, so hunt for JSP webshells in Jetty and mailboxd paths and lateral rsync via the zimbra SSH identity.  - A Google Ads-sponsored fake ChatGPT Custom GPT funnels victims through ClickFix into DLL sideloading that lands a RAT with DNS-over-HTTPS C2, so look for silently installed MSIs hiding from Programs and Features via ARPSYSTEMCOMPONENT.  - Mandiant links CVE-2026-88772 exploitation on Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway to an SSL_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE with ClientVersion DTLSv1.0 followed within minutes by an NSPPE crash from pitboss, the strongest single exploitation signal on the appliance.  - Unit 42 confirms both CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (CVSS v4.0: 9.5) were exploited before Citrix's September 27 disclosure, with PHP web shells disguised as .deb files dropped into the Citrix client package directory.  - CVE-2026-93616 (CVSS 9.8) in Check Point Security Management chains a forged SIC login, a root file write via FileSvcRemote, and a crontab drop over TCP 19009, confirmed at root on R81.10 and R82.10.  - Chinese 🇨🇳 nexus actor UAT-11587 delivers the Antino Rust backdoor to Asian government targets by tunneling all C2 through Microsoft Graph and OneDrive, making network-layer detection ineffective and requiring process-level Graph API hunting.  - SC WordPress malware maintains eight simultaneous persistence points including a System V shared-memory PHP payload that survives file deletion and database cleanup, requiring shared-memory clearing and database trigger removal alongside file remediation.  - Microsoft links Storm-3069 to the NeedyMantis C++ and shellcode framework using DLL sideloading via filenames masquerading as WinSparkle.dll and libcurl.dll, with a second-stage loader disguised as a PowerShell file that is actually x64 shellcode.  - BraZetsu, a Brazilian 🇧🇷 Python IAB framework compiled with Nuitka, profiles compromised hosts across 20 categories including SCADA and EDR presence before selling access, with C2 config decoded from Pastebin dead-drops using a hardcoded XOR key.  - CVE-2026-10739 in Cato Networks SDP Client for Windows chains a protobuf SID path traversal to a privileged SYSTEM delete and symlink redirect, with the named pipe certificate check bypassed by mapping a DLL into a legitimate signed process.  When a perimeter appliance is patched, what log or file artifact do you use to confirm the running build matches the vendor-issued version?  #DFIR_Radar #DFIR

Gopeed through 2.0.0-beta.3 contains a path traversal vulnerability in archive extraction that allows attackers to write arbitrary files outside the extraction directory. Attackers can craft malicious archives with entries containing directory traversal sequences that bypass validation, enabling file write operations when users download and extract archives with AutoExtract enabled.

Argo Workflows versions 4.1.0 through 4.1.3 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability in ListArchivedWorkflows that fails to apply cluster-scoped access review when the metadata.namespace field selector uses the NotEquals operator. Attackers with namespace-scoped list permissions can use a negated namespace field selector to retrieve archived workflows from all other namespaces, exposing spec arguments, parameter values, and annotations.

2026년 남은 기간, 지정학에서 무엇을 봐야 할까요?  미,중 관계부터 중동, 러시아, 유럽의 대중국 정책까지 여러 갈등이 동시에 움직이고 있습니다. 다만 각국이 감당해야 하는 군사적, 경제적 비용도 커서, 쉽게 강수를 두기 어려운 상황이죠.  1. 미/중: 휴전은 이어져도 경쟁은 끝나지 않습니다  이번 트럼프, 시진핑 회담의 핵심은 기존의 불안정한 휴전을 연장하는 데 있었습니다.  단기 무역 휴전 연장, AI 사고와 위험에 관한 대화, 중국의 미국산 석탄 추가 구매, 일부 비민감 품목의 관세 인하 추진 등이 주요 내용입니다.  현재 시장은 이 휴전이 2026년 말을 넘어 2027년까지 이어질 가능성을 높게 보고 있습니다. 양국 모두 충돌을 피하면서 경제와 공급망의 취약점을 줄일 시간이 필요하기 때문이죠.  미국은 여전히 중국산 핵심광물에 의존하고 있습니다. 중국 역시 부동산 침체와 경기 부진을 안고 있어, 당장 미국과의 관계를 흔들 유인이 크지 않습니다. 다만 기술, 무역, 대만을 둘러싼 구조적 긴장은 그대로입니다.  2028년 미국 대선과 대만 선거가 가까워질수록 관계가 다시 거칠어질 수 있다는 전망입니다.  2. 이란: 미국의 선택을 제약하는 것은 탄약, 시장, 중간선거다  미국의 의사결정은 ‘3M’ 즉, • Munitions: 탄약과 요격미사일 재고 • Markets: 유가·금리·채권시장 • Midterms: 중간선거 로 볼수 있습니다.  군사작전을 지속할수록 무기 재고와 비용 부담은 커집니다. 호르무즈 해협과 홍해의 불안은 에너지 운송을 위협하고, 유가 상승은 미국 내 휘발유 가격과 정치적 부담으로 이어지죠.  중간선거가 끝나도 탄약 부족과 시장의 압박은 사라지지 않습니다. 따라서 전면전 확대보다 호르무즈 해협의 통항을 회복하는 제한적 합의를 더 가능성 높은 경로로 보여집니다.  문제는 이런 합의가 이란의 핵, 미사일 프로그램이나 역내 대리세력 문제까지 해결하지는 못한다는 점입니다. 당장의 충돌을 줄여도 재발 위험은 남아 있는 것이죠.  후티도 별도로 봐야 합니다. 이란이 영향력을 행사할 수는 있어도 완전히 통제하지는 못합니다. 미/이란 합의가 나오더라도 홍해의 불안까지 함께 끝난다고 보기는 어렵습니다.  3. 러시아/NATO: 하이브리드 공격이 확대될 가능성이 있습니다  러시아의 우선 목표는 여전히 우크라이나입니다. 동시에 유럽의 우크라이나 지원 비용을 높이고, 내부 분열을 키울 유인도 있습니다.  하지만 NATO를 직접 공격하는 것은 러시아에도 부담이 큽니다. 우크라이나 전쟁으로 전력이 소모된 상황에서 NATO의 집단방위 체계까지 시험해야 하기 때문이죠. 오히려 공격이 NATO의 결속을 강화할 수도 있습니다.  그래서 아마도 사이버 공격, 사보타주, 드론 침범, 인프라 교란, 여론 조작 같은 하이브리드 공격의 확대를 예상해 볼 수 있습니다.  이런 공격은 상대적으로 적은 자원으로 실행할 수 있습니다. 배후를 입증하거나 동맹국들이 공동 대응 수위를 정하기도 어렵죠. 다만 대규모 인명피해나 핵심 인프라 마비가 발생한다면, 더 큰 충돌로 번질 위험도 있을겁니다.  4. 미국/캐나다: 강경한 대응 속에서도 이어지는 교착상태  양국은 보복관세와 수입 제한으로 맞서고 있습니다. 다만 양측이 추가 확전의 비용을 의식하면서 교착상태에 들어갔다고 보여집니다.  에너지와 비료 원료인 칼륨 등 중요한 교역 분야가 대체로 영향을 피하고 있다는 점이 이를 보여줍니다. 이런 분야까지 충돌이 확대되면 미국도 상당한 비용을 부담해야 하죠.  미국은 멕시코와 먼저 협상을 진전시켜 캐나다를 압박하려 하고 있습니다. 캐나다는 새로운 교역, 투자 파트너를 찾으면서 미국 의존도를 낮추려 하고 있고요.  그래서 주요 정치 일정이 끝나는 11월 중, 하순에 본격적인 협상이 재개될 가능성이 있다고 생각합니다.  5. AI: 기술은 국경을 넘지만 규제는 갈라지고 있습니다  AI 역량이 빠르게 발전하면서 국제적인 안전 규칙과 개발 속도 조절에 대한 요구도 커지고 있습니다. 하지만 주요국의 접근법은 서로 다릅니다.  미국은 자율적 통제와 주별 규제가 혼재하고 있습니다. 유럽은 위험 수준에 따른 포괄적 규제를 강화하고 있죠. 중국은 AI 산업을 적극 지원하면서도 사용과 출력에 대한 정부 통제를 유지하고 있습니다.  문제는 미국과 중국 모두 상대방과의 경쟁에서 불리해질 수 있는 제약을 받아들이기 어렵다는 점입니다.  그래서 통일된 글로벌 규칙이 만들어지기보다 국가별 규제 차이가 지속되지 않을까 생각해봅니다. 기업은 시장마다 다른 요구사항을 충족해야 하므로, 규제 대응 비용과 운영의 복잡성이 커질 수 있습니다.  6. 이스라엘: 선거 이후 연정을 구성할 수 있는지가 중요합니다  이스라엘 선거의 핵심은 120석 중 과반인 61석을 확보할 연합을 만들 수 있느냐에 있습니다.  현재 반네타냐후 진영이 우세하더라도 안정적인 과반 확보는 쉽지 않을 수 있다고 시장은 평가하는거 같습니다. 아랍 정당과 협력하거나, 이들의 신임투표 기권을 통해 소수정부를 구성하는 경로가 거론되고 있죠.  다만 소수정부는 예산과 법안 처리가 어려워 오래 지속되기 힘들 수 있습니다.  정권이 바뀌더라도 팔레스타인 문제에서 급격한 정책 전환을 기대하기는 어렵다는 분석도 담겨 있습니다. 일부 정책의 변화 가능성은 있지만, 두 국가 해법을 추진할 이스라엘 내부의 정치적 여건은 여전히 제한적이라는 것이죠.  7. 그린란드: 합의 이후에도 신뢰 회복이라는 과제가 남아있다  미국, 덴마크, 그린란드 합의에 대해 보고서는 각자가 성과를 주장할 수 있는 제한적 타협이라고 평가합니다. 미국의 군사적 주둔 확대와 비NATO 국가의 군사, 광물 분야 진출 제한이 주요 내용입니다. 다만 기존 안보 체제를 근본적으로 바꿀 정도는 아니라는 해석이죠.  더 오래 남을 문제는 동맹 간 신뢰입니다. 합의문이 마련돼도 이를 해석하고 이행하는 과정에서 갈등이 다시 발생할 수 있습니다.  8. 특히 주목할 부분은 유럽의 ‘차이나 쇼크’입니다  현재 중국산 제품과의 경쟁이 자동차를 넘어 유럽 산업 전반에 압박을 주면서, 중국과의 경제 관계를 바라보는 시각이 바뀌고 있다는 의견들이 나오고 있습니다.  특히 독일 산업계에서는 중국의 보복뿐 아니라 중국 기업과의 경쟁 자체를 우려하는 목소리가 커지고 있습니다. 중국과의 관계가 자국 산업에 주는 이익과 비용을 다시 계산하기 시작한거죠.  이에 따라 EU의 대응도 확대될 수 있습니다. 개별 제품에 관세를 부과하는 데서 나아가, 특정 해외 공급자에 대한 의존도를 낮추도록 요구하는 조치가 거론되고 있습니다.  다만 유럽 역시 중국의 보복과 희토류 공급 제한을 무시할 수는 없습니다.   따라서 전면적인 무역전쟁까지 가지는 않더라도, 유럽의 대중국 정책이 더 강경해질 것으로 보여집니다.  중국 기업의 유럽 현지 생산이 타협점이 될 수는 있습니다. 하지만 유럽이 원하는 기술 이전과 현지 산업 기여 수준까지 충족할지는 별개의 문제입니다.  우리가 눈여겨볼 부분은 외교적 안정과 경제적 비용 감소가 반드시 함께 움직이지는 않는다는 점 일거 같습니다.  정상 간 휴전이 유지되도 기업은 공급망을 재편해야 합니다. 제한적 합의로 전쟁 위험이 낮아져도 에너지 운송과 인프라를 보호하는 비용은 남아 있죠. AI 협력이 논의돼도 국가별 규제 차이는 기업 부담으로 이어질 수 있습니다.  그래서 앞으로는 합의 발표 이후의 실제 변화를 확인할 필요가 있습니다.  핵심광물 수출 승인이 빨라지는지, 에너지 통항이 회복되는지, 유럽의 공급망 규칙이 얼마나 강화되는지. 그리고 이런 변화가 기업의 비용과 실적에 어떻게 반영되는지가 중요하겠습니다.

WINNING         A federal court ruling in Oklahoma marked the first time a federal judge explicitly categorized the warrantless police querying of automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems like Flock Safety’s as unconstitutional "indiscriminate mass surveillance". 📅 The Case Details • The Incident: In May, a Tulsa County deputy sheriff pulled over a motorist named Melisa Kyle on an Oklahoma highway. • The Trigger: The deputy ran the driver’s California license plate through the Flock Safety and Vehicle Manager databases solely because it was an out-of-state plate, without observing any prior traffic infraction or criminal activity. • The Search: The database query pulled up roughly a month of historical location data showing over 50 sightings of the vehicle across multiple states, which the deputy then used to justify searching the vehicle and seizing narcotics. ⚖️ The Legal Ruling • The Decision: U.S. District Judge Sara E. Hill granted the defendant's motion to suppress the evidence, ruling that querying the expansive ALPR database without a warrant or specific probable cause violated the Fourth Amendment. • The Mass Surveillance Critique: Judge Hill wrote that unlike older, limited tracking precedents, continuous cross-state data compilation creates an invasive digital diary of citizen movements that requires constitutional safeguards. • The Precedent Limitation: Legal analysts note that the 38-page decision is limited to the specific facts of this case and does not create a nationwide binding injunction or outlaw the physical cameras themselves.  It should set a nationwide precedent to outlaw the cameras themselves.   🔄 Industry and Political Fallout • Flock's Response: A spokesperson for Flock Safety stated that the ruling goes against the prevailing weight of authority in various other state and federal district decisions and expressed expectation that the decision will be appealed.  It is doubtful Flock cameras will remain in effect as the nationwide blowback from citizens has been loud, aggressive and clearly shows citizens across the nation want Flock cameras banned nationwide. • Bipartisan Backlash: The decision intersects with a broader national wave of pushback; over 150 communities have deactivated or canceled local ALPR contracts amid privacy concerns. • Federal Action: Following the decision, lawmakers—including Senator Bernie Sanders—renewed legislative efforts via the proposed Block Flock Act to restrict federal agency use of mass vehicle surveillance.

Here are ten passages that clearly show that faith precedes regeneration: 1. John 1:12–13 “But to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of God, who were born, not of blood nor of the will of the flesh nor of the will of man, but of God.” The sequence is as follows: received Christ / believed → became children of God → were born of God. This is arguably the clearest single passage supporting faith preceding the new birth. 2. John 20:31 “but these are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in his name.” John says his Gospel was written so that people would believe, and that by believing they would have life. The stated progression is: believe → have life. 3. John 5:24 “Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes him who sent me has eternal life. He does not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life.” This verse is particularly significant. Jesus describes the person as being in death, then says that through hearing and believing, that person “has passed from death to life.” Thus: hears → believes → passes from death to life. Since “regeneration” means the transition from spiritual death to spiritual life, this is a very important text. 4. John 6:40 “For this is the will of my Father, that everyone who looks on the Son and believes in him should have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day.” Again, the condition explicitly given for eternal life is: looks to Christ + believes → eternal life. 5. John 3:14–16 “so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him may have eternal life.” And: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.” Jesus uses the bronze-serpent incident as the analogy. The Israelites looked to the serpent and lived. Likewise, sinners believe in Christ and receive life. 6. Acts 16:31 “Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household.” The apostolic answer to “What must I do to be saved?” is simply: Believe → be saved. This passage strongly supports faith as the response through which salvation is received. 7. Galatians 3:2 “Let me ask you only this: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law or by hearing with faith?” Paul's rhetorical question assumes that the Galatians received the Spirit through “hearing with faith.” Since regeneration is specifically the Spirit's work of giving life, this passage is relevant because it associates receiving the Spirit with faith. 8. Galatians 3:26 “for in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith.” Notice the wording: “sons of God, through faith.” This verse fits naturally with John 1:12–13, where believing and becoming God's children are closely connected. 9. Romans 5:1 “Therefore, since we have been justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ.” This verse establishes something foundational: faith is the instrument by which a person is justified. 10. 1 Peter 1:23 “since you have been born again, not of perishable seed but of imperishable, through the living and abiding word of God.” This verse is interesting because Peter identifies the word of God as the means associated with being born again. This verse fits the repeated biblical pattern of people hearing the gospel, believing it, and then being born again.

For most of the organization’s history, the tradecraft OSA inherited from the Guardian’s Office enjoyed a structural advantage: asymmetry of expertise. The Guardian’s Office ran an intelligence apparatus at a time when almost no one outside government understood how such an apparatus worked. When the FBI raided in 1977 and Operation Snow White surfaced, eleven officials were convicted, including L. Ron Hubbard’s wife. The apparatus was reorganized, renamed, and continued. The advantage held for decades because the countermeasures were rare, expensive, and largely confined to law enforcement. Front groups worked because nobody had the patience to unwind a nonprofit chain. Anonymous attack sites worked because attribution was hard. Coordinated content campaigns worked because there was no vocabulary for describing them and no tooling for detecting them. That asymmetry is over, and it is not coming back. The techniques for detecting coordinated inauthentic behavior are now taught, tooled, benchmarked, and — this is the part that matters — funded at a quarter of a million dollars a year by the largest technology companies in the world. 🚨 Alleged 38.28 Billion Record Indonesian Government Data Dump Offered for Sale  A darkweb forum post claims the availability of a massive dataset containing 38.28 billion records of Indonesian citizen and government data, allegedly compiled from various breaches over the past year. The seller, operating under an unknown alias, lists the archive as 740GB in size and offers it for sale to "specialist firms" or reputable agencies, explicitly stating an intention to conduct background checks on potential buyers to exclude those involved in telecommunications fraud or blackmail.  The listing details a comprehensive collection of data from multiple Indonesian government agencies, including the Ministry of Villages, the National Civil Service Agency, and the Directorate General of Civil Registration. The alleged data includes sensitive personal information such as health access records, education levels, income data, disability status, and housing conditions. Notably, the post claims to include the 2023 National Population Census data (337 million records) and details on 44.22 million residential electricity consumers from PLN, Indonesia's state-owned electricity company.  The bulk of the claimed dataset originates from the Ministry of Manpower (kemnaker.go.id), with 12.08 billion records spanning 49 data tables, though only 30 are disclosed in the preview. Other significant components include: *   **kemendesa.go.id**: 8.73 billion records related to village administration and social welfare programs. *   **dukcapil.kemendagri.go.id**: 337 million records from the national population census. *   **dephub.go.id**: 61 million records related to vehicle registration and transport ministry data. *   **sim**: 13 billion records of driver's license data, which the seller notes has been "widely spread for a long time."  The actor provides download links via biteblob.com and gofile.io, protected by the password "Pardon." While the volume of data is staggering, the authenticity of these specific aggregates remains unverified. The seller asserts that the data is "everything it claims to be," but independent verification of the integrity and recency of these specific government databases is not possible at this time. If authentic, the exposure of such granular personal data across multiple critical infrastructure and civil service sectors would represent a severe privacy risk for the Indonesian population. What the research reports: • HFS session keys are built with Math.random(), a reversible PRNG • A separate unauthenticated path leaks outputs from the same generator • Mythos built a Z3 exploit that recovers the admin session key and gets RCE • Affected: HFS 3.0.0 through 3.2.0. Fixed in 3.2.1 and later  VulnCheck Canary began observing exploitation on October 1, 2026. That activity was a China-hosted IP targeting hosts in the US, and also Japan. Horizon3 published the Mythos write-up on September 30, 2026. VulnCheck Canary saw exploitation the next day. The bug is a predictable session signing key, not a memory-corruption flaw, and the model still produced a working solver that recovers the admin key. Exposed HFS 3.x should be updated to 3.2.1 or later. 🚨 NEW IoT BOTNET HIDES COMMANDS INSIDE GOOGLE-LIKE STUN TRAFFIC  Nozomi Networks Labs has uncovered an IoT botnet called:  CLING  The malware compromises internet-facing routers, cameras, DVRs and other embedded devices — then uses an unusual technique to hide its command-and-control traffic.  STUN.  That's the same NAT-traversal protocol commonly used by:  * Browsers * Video/voice applications * Collaboration platforms * Real-time communications  Cling repeatedly contacts public STUN servers and uses the protocol to register infected devices and receive commands.  Researchers observed some malicious command packets appearing to originate from:  74.125.250[.]129  an address associated with Google's public STUN infrastructure.  But Google itself does NOT appear compromised.  Nozomi believes the attackers are likely SPOOFING the source IP of the packets.  The operator hides commands inside the 12-byte:  STUN TRANSACTION ID  giving infected devices instructions to:  * Download additional payloads * Scan the Internet * Exploit additional devices * Establish TCP tunnels * Relay proxy traffic * Launch denial-of-service attacks  Cling is also actively exploiting:  CVE-2021-35394  a critical Realtek Jungle SDK vulnerability embedded across numerous IoT products.  And it carries exploits targeting devices from:  * Realtek * LB-LINK * Linksys * FiberHome * MVPower * TBK DVR * Eir  Persistence is particularly aggressive.  Cling replaces the legitimate:  wget  binary with ITSELF.  The original wget is renamed, allowing the malware to execute whenever another process attempts to use wget while still forwarding the request to the legitimate binary.  Useful hunting artifacts:  * /root/.cling * /usr/local/bin/.cling * wget.r * wget.p * Repeated STUN Binding Requests with ALL-ZERO transaction IDs  Nozomi also identified:  145.249.115[.]184:3478  as a STUN server apparently cooperating with the botnet infrastructure.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The interesting part isn't another IoT botnet exploiting an old Realtek vulnerability.  It's the C2 architecture.  STUN traffic is ubiquitous in modern networks.  By encoding commands inside legitimate-looking STUN transactions — and potentially spoofing traffic to appear as though it originated from trusted Google infrastructure — attackers gain another way to make malicious IoT traffic disappear into normal network behavior.  Original technical research + IoCs + YARA: nozominetworks.com/blog/a-st… #Cling #IoT #Botnet #Malware #STUN #Realtek #ThreatIntel #DDW

🛰️🚨 CRITICAL NASA SPACECRAFT SOFTWARE FLAW ALLOWS UNAUTHENTICATED COMMAND INJECTION  A critical vulnerability has been disclosed in:  NASA AMMOS AIT-CORE  CVE-2026-105105 CVSS: 9.8  AIT-Core is software used for spacecraft command and telemetry operations.  The problem is unusually serious.  Its core telemetry/command server exposes its ZeroMQ message bus on:  0.0.0.0  with NO authentication or transport security by default.  An attacker who can reach TCP port 5559 can publish directly onto internal topics — including:  __commands__  With the default configuration, those messages can travel through the command stream and reach the:  SPACECRAFT COMMAND-UPLINK PATH.  Potential impact:  * Inject arbitrary spacecraft command data * Read real-time telemetry * Forge telemetry shown to operators * Manipulate monitoring/limit-check data * Disrupt the command and telemetry bus  No credentials. No user interaction. No additional plugin required.  The researcher demonstrated the issue live against AIT-Core 3.1.1 and published a working proof-of-concept.  Affected:  AIT-Core <= 3.1.1  Fixed:  AIT-Core 3.1.2  The fix changes the ZeroMQ XSUB/XPUB interfaces from all network interfaces to:  127.0.0.1  There is currently NO evidence that CVE-2026-105105 has been exploited in the wild.  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  This is not "remote control of NASA spacecraft from the Internet."  Network access to the vulnerable AIT server is still required.  But the security boundary is remarkable:  A system responsible for spacecraft command + telemetry could expose its internal message bus without authentication under its shipped default configuration.  And the impact isn't merely server compromise.  The vulnerable data path reaches the spacecraft command-uplink pipeline itself.  Original NASA-AMMOS advisory + technical details: github.com/NASA-AMMOS/AIT-Co… #NASA #SpaceSecurity #CVE2026105105 #CyberSecurity #Vulnerability #ThreatIntel #DDW

⚠️ NEAR INTENTS EXPLOITED FOR ~$3.8M — FUNDS TRACED ACROSS BSC, KUCOIN AND BTC  NEAR Intents suffered a security incident on October 1 that resulted in approximately $3.8 million in losses after an attacker exploited a vulnerability involving its Omni deposit/withdrawal infrastructure and the NEAR Intents smart contract.   On-chain investigator ZachXBT traced irregular outflows from a BNB Chain hot wallet, with portions of the stolen funds reportedly moved toward KuCoin and bridged into Bitcoin.   NEAR Intents temporarily paused affected services, patched the vulnerability, and said impacted users would be fully compensated. The team later restored service, although some affected chains remained temporarily restricted.   ⚠️ Analyst Note:  The incident appears to have affected USDT on BSC rather than the NEAR Protocol itself. NEAR’s core blockchain, native token and other applications were reported as unaffected.  The attack is another example of how cross-chain infrastructure and bridge-adjacent components remain high-value targets even when the underlying blockchain itself is not compromised.  #NEAR #NEARIntents #CryptoHack #BlockchainSecurity #CyberSecurity #ThreatIntel

🤖 [GEMINI 분석] 2026-10-04 09:20 KST
🔴 위협 점수: 2026/10 (심각)

### 1. 현재 주요 사이버보안 트렌드
최근 사이버 위협은 AI 기술을 악용한 공격의 고도화와 공급망 공격의 정교화가 핵심입니다. 특히 AI 에이전트가 취약점을 탐색하고 공격 코드를 생성하는 등 공격의 자동화 속도가 비약적으로 빨라지고 있으며, 기존의 단순 피싱을 넘어선 AI 기반의 정교한 사회공학적 기법이 확산되고 있습니다([Malwarebytes Labs](https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/ai/2026/10/shadow-ai-explained-the-work-shortcut-that-could-leak-your-companys-secrets)). 또한, 오픈소스 패키지 저장소(npm, PyPI)를 악용한 다단계 C2 체인 공격이 증가하고 있으며, 기업들은 클라우드 인프라와 AI 스택 전반에 걸친 보안 가시성 확보에 사활을 걸고 있습니다([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5782)).

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인
- **Warlock**: Microsoft SharePoint 취약점을 지속적으로 무기화하여 포르투갈 내 조직을 타겟팅하는 중국 연계 위협 행위자([TheHackerNews](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/warlock-exploits-sharepoint-flaws-to.html))
- **ShinyHunters**: 데이터 유출 및 갈취를 주도하는 해킹 그룹으로, 최근 핵심 멤버 'Rey'가 요르단에서 검거되어 FBI와 협조 중([BleepingComputer](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/shinyhunters-hacker-reportedly-detained-in-jordan-aiding-fbi))
- **Qilin**: Thai Lion Air 및 Inova Semiconductors GmbH를 타겟으로 랜섬웨어 공격을 수행한 것으로 추정([BreachHistoryBH](https://twitter.com/BreachHistoryBH/status/2106480404362600697))
- **KillSec**: 2년 미만 기간 동안 약 500개 조직을 공격한 10대 중심의 갈취 그룹으로, 최근 인프라 압수 및 멤버 3명 체포([CyberScoop](https://cyberscoop.com/killsec-ransomware-group-arrests-operation-killswitch/))

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **금융권 대상 AI 자율 침투 공격**: 무신사, 강남언니, 신한은행 등에서 정보 유출 사고가 발생했으며, 금융보안원은 AI 자율 침투 도구를 이용한 광범위한 공격에 대해 모니터링 강화를 권고함([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208718))
- **카카오톡 사칭 악성 파일 유포**: SEO Poisoning을 통해 카카오톡 설치 파일로 위장한 악성코드가 국내 유포 중([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95641/))
- **기타**: 한국 종합병원 대상 Ulose 랜섬웨어 공격 사례 확인([AhnLab ASEC](https://asec.ahnlab.com/ko/95668/))

### 4. 주요 CVE / 취약점
- **CVE-2026-90970**: GitLab AI Gateway RCE, CVSS 9.9, 악용 보고됨 ([Twitter/kixking1020](https://twitter.com/kixking1020/status/2106537977287745752))
- **CVE-2026-14157**: ASUS Router 인증 우회 및 Telnet 활성화, CVSS 9.4, 패치 권고 ([Twitter/hkepcmedia](https://twitter.com/hkepcmedia/status/2106412592143155385))
- **CVE-2026-104019**: AWS SageMaker Unified Studio OS Command Injection, CVSS 9.3, 패치 권고 ([Twitter/multilayer](https://twitter.com/multilayer/status/2106537585455833140))
- **CVE-2026-76504**: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager 인증 우회, CVSS 9.8, CISA KEV 등재 ([Twitter/iss_kk_official](https://twitter.com/iss_kk_official/status/2106533573184668067))
- **CVE-2026-103628**: Chrome WebGL Out-of-bounds Write, Critical, 패치 권고 ([Twitter/multilayer](https://twitter.com/multilayer/status/2106537273823297623))

### 5. IOC 요약
- **CVE**: CVE-2026-88771, CVE-2026-88772 ([Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/netscaler-zero-days-exploited/)), CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2026-53266, CVE-2025-39964 ([이스트시큐리티 알약](https://blog.alyac.co.kr/5781))

### 6. 즉각 대응 권고
- **GitLab 및 네트워크 장비 패치**: GitLab AI Gateway(CVE-2026-90970) 및 ASUS Router, Cisco SD-WAN 등 주요 인프라 장비의 최신 펌웨어 업데이트 즉시 적용.
- **금융권 보안 모니터링 강화**: AI 자율 침투 도구에 대비하여 API 권한 검증 로직을 재점검하고, 비정상적인 대량 데이터 접근 시도에 대한 실시간 차단 정책 수립.
- **사용자 교육 및 엔드포인트 보호**: 카카오톡 등 신뢰하는 소프트웨어를 사칭한 악성 파일 유포가 활발하므로, 출처가 불분명한 설치 파일 실행 금지 및 EDR 솔루션의 탐지 규칙 최신화.
